title: Cambridge moves to make sex work safer, stops short of decriminalization
author: Fiona Bright Holton
bullets: Local News The policy calls for a crisis hotline, anti-poverty measures, and making sex work a low priority for police — but stops short of decriminalization.
Cambridge City Council voted Monday night to make sex work safer in the city.

David L Ryan/Globe Staff Cambridge City Council voted Monday night to make sex work safer in the city, directing officials to establish a crisis hotline for sex workers, pursue anti-poverty measures, and discourage local law enforcement from arresting and prosecuting them.
